title: Bodies, Betrayals & Bangers
description: Bodies and babies, diet disasters, famous backstabs, three decades of bangers, sci-fi love stories, and 90s–2010s nostalgia — every fact web-verified.

questions.question: The event known as 'water breaking' is the rupture of this fluid-filled membrane surrounding the fetus.
This largest muscle in the human body forms the shape of the buttocks.
These harmless 'practice' uterine contractions during pregnancy are named after an English physician who first described them in 1872.
About 3 millimeters long, this middle ear bone is the smallest in the human body.
This U-shaped bone in the neck is unique because it doesn't connect directly to any other bone.
Queens housewife Jean Nidetch founded this weight-loss company in 1963; it later became famous for a Points system.
This evidence-backed diet, inspired by 1960s Greece and Italy eating patterns, consistently ranks #1 overall in US News' best diets.
Beyoncé drank this lemonade, maple syrup and cayenne pepper detox for a 2006 film role.
The FDA pulled half of this 1990s miracle diet-drug duo in 1997 after reports of heart valve damage.
Eli Lilly makes this diabetes drug — the first dual GIP and GLP-1 agonist — whose weight-loss counterpart is Zepbound.
For 30 pieces of silver, this disciple identified Jesus to authorities with a kiss.
This Revolutionary War general plotted to surrender West Point to the British in 1780 before fleeing to enemy lines.
This Mean Girls queen bee terrorizes her school with a vicious notebook called the Burn Book.
Named after a 1944 film in which a husband dims the lamps, this tactic makes victims doubt reality.
This son of King David led a rebellion and met his end when his hair caught in an oak tree.
Mark Ronson and Bruno Mars topped the charts for 14 weeks with this funk smash — 'Don't believe me, just watch.'
Danish-Norwegian group Aqua sang this 1997 hit — 'You can brush my hair, undress me everywhere.'
This first single from Ricky Martin's 1999 English-language album is credited with launching the Latin pop explosion in America.
Gwen Stefani's 2005 cheerleader-style stomp was the first song to sell one million paid digital downloads in the U.S.
The Verve lost all royalties to this 1997 hit over a Stones sample dispute until rights returned in 2019.
James Cameron's 2009 epic set on the moon Pandora became the highest-grossing film of all time.
In this 2004 film, Jim Carrey hires a firm to erase memories of his ex, played by Kate Winslet.
questions.answer: What is Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind?

questions.question: In this 2013 film, Joaquin Phoenix's writer falls for an OS voiced by Scarlett Johansson.
In this 2016 Denis Villeneuve film, Amy Adams' linguist tries to communicate with seven-limbed aliens called heptapods.
In this 2006 Alfonso Cuarón film, two decades of infertility have left humanity childless — until a woman becomes pregnant.
At its peak this video rental chain had about 9,000 stores; today just one U.S. location remains, in Bend, Oregon.
Introduced with Office 97, this animated paperclip asked, 'It looks like you're writing a letter.'
From an MTV studio in Times Square, Carson Daly hosted this countdown show while fans screamed outside the window.
Zynga's 2009 Facebook game had players tending virtual crops and nagging friends for help; at peak, 83 million monthly players.
Nullsoft's 1997 MP3 player promised that it 'really whips the llama's ass' — until AOL bought and sidelined it.
